s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic hematochezia in an immunocompromised patient with gastrointestinal polyps and mixed inflammatory infiltrate
salient_findings: Multiple semisessile polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon
Eroded surface mucosa with reactive hyperplastic glands and dense mixed inflammatory infiltrate
Histiocytes with basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions
key_facts: 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia
Receiving maintenance therapy with 6-mercaptopurine, methotrexate, vincristine, and dexamethasone
Intermittently neutropenic and consistently lymphopenic
Two to three loose bowel movements per day with mixed blood
Denies abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions
Stool studies negative for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus
Colonoscopy showed multiple polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon
Histologic examination revealed eroded surface mucosa and dense mixed inflammatory infiltrate
Histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions
Inclusions were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains

shortlist.label: Malacoplakia
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic examination revealed eroded surface mucosa and dense mixed inflammatory infiltrate with basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions, consistent with Malacoplakia

shortlist.label: Neutropenic colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is intermittently neutropenic and presents with hematochezia and mixed inflammatory infiltrate

shortlist.label: Hemorrhagic colitis due to 6-mercaptopurine
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is receiving 6-mercaptopurine, which is a known cause of hemorrhagic colitis

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is immunocompromised and presents with gastrointestinal symptoms, although stool studies were negative

shortlist.label: Graft-versus-host disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of immunocompromise and is at risk for graft-versus-host disease, which can cause gastrointestinal symptoms

raw.rationale: The presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes that are strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains is characteristic of Malacoplakia, which is a rare inflammatory condition often associated with immunocompromised states

rejected.label: Neutropenic colitis
rejected.why: While the patient is intermittently neutropenic, the histologic findings do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Hemorrhagic colitis due to 6-mercaptopurine
rejected.why: The colonoscopy and histologic findings do not match the typical presentation of this condition

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus colitis
rejected.why: Stool studies and histologic examination did not reveal evidence of cytomegalovirus infection

rejected.label: Graft-versus-host disease
rejected.why: There is no mention of a transplant or other risk factors for graft-versus-host disease
